section_summary: This section documents the release, content, and domestic and international reactions to the Economic Stabilization Board's draft Five-Year Plan for Japanese Economic Rehabilitation (1948–1952), designed to return Japan to 1930–1934 living and production standards. It contains serialized press texts of the draft plan, Japanese editorial commentaries and committee regulations forwarded by USPOLAD Tokyo, and high-level evaluations by Japanese leaders and U.S. diplomats debating the necessity of American aid and economic controls. The section concludes with State Department records concerning accelerating Japanese population growth, U.S. congressional inquiries regarding occupation economic policies, and Chinese editorial protests in the Ta Kung Pao against rebuilding Japan's industrial capacity.

subfiles.about: Concluding text and summary table of Section I of the Economic Stabilization Board's draft five-year plan for Japanese economic rehabilitation.
subfiles.summary: Presents planned 1952 targets for production, trade, and living standards, emphasizing that self-sufficiency requires curbing inflation, foreign aid, regional stability, and power rehabilitation.
subfiles.title: Draft Five-Year Plan for Japanese Economic Rehabilitation: Section I (Concluded) and Goal for 1952

subfiles.about: English translation and Japanese clipping of a Nihon Keizai Shimbun editorial analyzing the Economic Stabilization Board's draft five-year rehabilitation program.
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Analyzes the Economic Stabilization Board's five-year plan, advising the Planning Committee to deliberate carefully, revise unrealistic assumptions, address hidden unemployment, and establish concrete policy endorsements lacking in the draft.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 326: Contents of Economic Rehabilitation Program (The Nihon Keizai Shimbun, May 18, 1948)

subfiles.about: English translation and Japanese clipping of an Asahi Shimbun editorial urging thorough scrutiny and prompt implementation of the Economic Rehabilitation Program.
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Welcomes the draft economic rehabilitation program but warns of serious weaknesses, including the lack of currency and financial planning, transport bottlenecks, inadequate labor representation on the planning committee, and unemployment risks.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 3 to Despatch No. 326: Immediate Establishment of 'The Program' Is Desired (The Asahi Shimbun, May 18, 1948)

subfiles.about: Nippon Times press clipping translating a Yomiuri editorial on the Economic Stabilization Board's five-year rehabilitation program.
subfiles.summary: Criticizes the Economic Stabilization Board's five-year draft as an abstract calculation lacking concrete foundation, omitting required foreign credit amounts and timing, and ignoring monetary planning and inflation risks.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 4 to Despatch No. 326: Economic Rehabilitation Program (Yomiuri Press Comments, Nippon Times, May 19, 1948)

subfiles.about: Nippon Times press clipping translating a Mainichi editorial evaluating the Economic Stabilization Board's five-year rehabilitation program.
subfiles.summary: Commends the drafters' efforts while pointing out vulnerabilities, including vague relations between capital needs and national income distribution, uncertain premises, and neglect of the housing crisis.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 5 to Despatch No. 326: Significance of Economic Rehabilitation Program (Mainichi Press Comments, Nippon Times, May 19, 1948)

subfiles.about: Editorial from the Nippon Times evaluating the Economic Stabilization Board's draft five-year plan for economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: Welcomes the five-year plan as a concrete recovery target but cautions that population estimates must be revised upward in line with the Strike Report, requiring targets to be realistically adjusted.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 6 to Despatch No. 326: The Five-Year Plan (Nippon Times Editorial, May 20, 1948)

subfiles.about: English translation of an article from the Communist newspaper Akahata condemning the government's economic recovery program as capitalist exploitation.
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Denounces the rehabilitation program as a capitalist scheme to exploit workers and farmers, maintain low wages, enrich monopolies, restore the Emperor system, and lower living standards while demanding doubled labor productivity.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 7 to Despatch No. 326: Economic Recovery Program (Akahata, May 21, 1948)

subfiles.about: Regulations governing the Japanese Economic Rehabilitation Planning Committee and an official roster of its appointed members and officers.
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Presents regulations enacted April 28, 1948, establishing the Economic Rehabilitation Planning Committee under the Economic Stabilization Board, accompanied by an April 21, 1948 roster of government, political, business, and labor members.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 8 to Despatch No. 326: Regulations and Membership of the Japanese Economic Rehabilitation Planning Committee

subfiles.about: Complete five-part serialization in the Nippon Times of the Economic Stabilization Board's draft five-year plan for Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: Serializes the draft five-year plan prepared by the Economic Stabilization Board to restore Japan's economy to roughly 1930-34 living standards by 1952. Outlines concrete targets for mining and manufacturing, energy development, food supply, foreign trade, transportation, and shipbuilding, while detailing employment needs and real national income projections. Emphasizes that successful implementation depends on curbing inflation, securing foreign credits and raw materials, and expanding trade across East Asia.
subfiles.title: 5-Year Recovery Plan: Draft of Measures Compiled by Economic Stabilization Board Released (Nippon Times, May 18-22, 1948)

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting and evaluating Japanese reactions to the Economic Rehabilitation Plan and urging continued American aid and economic controls.
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports views of Shigeto Tsuru, Hisato Ichimada, Hisaakira Kano, and Ichiro Ishikawa on the economic recovery plan, emphasizing the necessity of American aid and economic controls while noting demographic discrepancies with the Strike Report.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 352: Comments Concerning Japanese Economic Rehabilitation Plan

subfiles.about: English translation and Japanese text of an article by Shigeto Tsuru criticizing the draft economic rehabilitation program for omitting economic controls.
subfiles.summary: Argues that capital accumulation for rehabilitation requires suppressing consumption through strict allocation, price controls, and rationing, cautioning against a laissez-faire approach and urging a unified national guiding principle.
subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch No. 352: For Accomplishing Long-Range Program (Translation and Japanese text of article by Shigeto Tsuru, The Asahi Shimbun, May 18, 1948)

subfiles.about: Letter transmitting a published article on economic recovery in Japan to Representative Howard H. Buffett.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Acting Chief, Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs, Department of State
keywords: Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Transmits a copy of Whitman's published January 1948 Military Government Journal article on Japanese economic recovery in response to Representative Buffett's telephone request.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Representative Howard H. Buffett
subfiles.to: Howard Homan Buffett, House of Representatives

subfiles.about: Telegram summarizing an editorial from the Chinese newspaper Ta Kung Pao opposing U.S. policy to rebuild Japan's prewar industrial level.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Ta Kung Pao editorial warning that rebuilding Japan's industrial and living standards to pre-war levels threatens China's security, and demanding Allied consultation, democratic reform, and reparations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1377 from Shanghai: Ta Kung Pao Editorial on U.S. Policy in Japan

subfiles.about: Memorandum summarizing Economic Stabilization Board population projections and noting the absence of birth control planning.
subfiles.from: Marshall Green, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Economic Stabilization Board demographic projections showing population reaching 85.3 million by 1953 and notes lack of population control policies.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Population Estimates
